title: The Teeth
question: Which type of tooth is it?
lines: You use these front teeth to bite into an apple. Name them.
Watch the glowing teeth at the very front of the upper jaw.
Which type of tooth is glowing?
Canines are the pointed teeth right beside them.
These flat, chisel-shaped teeth are made for cutting.
It's B. Incisors.
Why it matters: adults have eight, four on top and four below.

title: The Teeth
question: How many of these do adults have?
lines: Between your pointed and grinding teeth sit the premolars.
Watch the glowing teeth between the canines and the big molars.
How many of these teeth does an adult have?
Adults have 12 molars, counting wisdom teeth, but those are different.
Two in each quarter of the mouth makes eight.
It's D. Eight.
Why it matters: premolars replace the baby molars.

title: The Teeth
question: What's their nickname?
lines: Two pointed teeth have a nickname that sounds like the eyes.
Watch the glowing teeth in the upper jaw.
What's their nickname?
Wisdom teeth are the back molars.
The pointed upper canines are called the eyeteeth.
It's C. Eyeteeth.
Why it matters: canines have the longest roots and tear food.

title: The Teeth
question: Which teeth are glowing?
lines: Two small teeth sit right at the front of your lower jaw.
Watch the glowing teeth at the center of the bottom row.
Which teeth are glowing?
The upper central incisors are larger and in the top row.
These two are in the middle of the lower jaw.
It's A. The lower central incisors.
Why it matters: incisors cut food; these are the smallest teeth.

title: The Teeth
question: Which teeth do the grinding?
lines: Some of your teeth are built to crush, not cut.
Watch the glowing teeth at the back of the mouth.
Which teeth do the grinding?
Premolars sit in front of them and do some crushing too.
The broad flat teeth at the back are the molars.
It's D. The molars.
Why it matters: their flat tops crush food before you swallow.
